Methodology & sources

How we check every date.

A deadline tracker is only useful if you can trust it. Here's where our dates come from, what the labels mean, and what we do when something changes or turns out to be wrong.

Where our dates come from

We rank sources in this order and always link to the highest one we can find:

  1. The law itself: legislation.gov.uk, the EU Official Journal (EUR-Lex), ICAO standards.
  2. The regulator: GOV.UK guidance, the Environment Agency, SEPA, Natural Resources Wales, NIEA, HMRC, the European Commission.
  3. Recognised experts: classification societies, law firms and verifiers. We use these only to understand the rules, or when no official text exists yet, and then the deadline is labelled "Date to verify".

Every deadline card shows when we last checked it and links to its source, so you can see the evidence yourself.

What the labels mean

LabelWhat it means
Confirmed
(no label on the card)		The date is set in law or official guidance, and we've checked it against that source.
Date to verifySources agree on the date, but we haven't yet seen it in an official text, or official sources disagree. The card explains what to check.
ExpectedAnnounced by government, but not yet in law.
ChangedThe date or rule has moved. The card shows the old and new position.

How we keep it current

  • Every month we check each regulator's news and guidance pages before the "What changed this month" email goes out.
  • Every 90 days at most we re-check every deadline against its source, even if nothing seems to have changed.
  • When something moves we update the deadline, log it on the What changed list with the old and new position, and include it in the next email.

How we decide "who it affects"

Each deadline says which sectors and company sizes it applies to, based on the scheme's scope rules: thresholds such as ship tonnage, thermal input, import value or staff numbers. These are summaries. If you're near a threshold, read the scheme guide and the official source, or ask your regulator.

Editorial independence

Partners and sponsors pay for clearly labelled space. They never see deadline content in advance, can't ask for changes, and don't influence which schemes we cover. A partner listing isn't an endorsement.

Corrections

If you think something is wrong, please report it. We aim to check every report within two working days. Confirmed corrections are fixed straight away and logged on the What changed list.

What we don't do

Compliance Clock is information, not legal or compliance advice. We don't file anything on your behalf, and your regulator's own guidance always takes priority. See our terms.
